column1: # One row per column the implemented tools write: the Picard metrics class, the column, its type
# (int, float or string) and a definition written from the Picard 3.5.0 behaviour the tool
# reproduces. Histogram columns have no metrics class; their first field is the Picard program
# name instead, and a label that varies by accumulation unit, orientation or library is written
# with a * for the varying part. Tab separated; lines starting with # are skipped.

column4: definition

Median insert size (absolute TLEN) of the counted pairs in this row's PAIR_ORIENTATION and accumulation unit. Half-integer when the pair count is even and the two middle sizes differ by an odd number.
Most frequent insert size; the smallest one on a tie.
Median of the absolute distances from the median insert size. About SD / 1.4826 for a normal distribution.
Smallest insert size seen. Usually an alignment artefact rather than a real fragment.
Largest insert size seen. A very large value points to an artefact or a rearrangement.

Mean of the insert sizes up to median + DEVIATIONS (default 10) x MAD, or up to HISTOGRAM_WIDTH if given. Only the upper tail is cut; small sizes stay in. MIN_HISTOGRAM_WIDTH raises the computed width but is ignored when HISTOGRAM_WIDTH is set.

Sample standard deviation (n - 1) of the insert sizes kept after the upper-tail cut described under MEAN_INSERT_SIZE. ? for a single pair; 0 when HISTOGRAM_WIDTH sits below the smallest insert size and nothing is kept.

Number of pairs in this orientation and unit, counted once per template from the second-of-pair read. A pair counts only if both mates are mapped to the same contig, TLEN is not 0, neither record is secondary or supplementary, and the read is not a duplicate unless INCLUDE_DUPLICATES is set. The count is taken before the upper-tail cut.
FR (mates face each other), RF (mates face away) or TANDEM (same strand). An orientation gets a row only when it holds at least MINIMUM_PCT (default 0.05) of the unit's pairs.
Width of the smallest symmetric window around the median that holds 10% of the pairs.
Width of the smallest symmetric window around the median that holds 20% of the pairs.
Width of the smallest symmetric window around the median that holds 30% of the pairs.
Width of the smallest symmetric window around the median that holds 40% of the pairs.
Width of the smallest symmetric window around the median that holds 50% of the pairs.
Width of the smallest symmetric window around the median that holds 60% of the pairs.
Width of the smallest symmetric window around the median that holds 70% of the pairs. Half of it approximates the SD of a normal distribution.
Width of the smallest symmetric window around the median that holds 80% of the pairs.
Width of the smallest symmetric window around the median that holds 90% of the pairs.
Width of the smallest symmetric window around the median that holds 95% of the pairs.
Width of the smallest symmetric window around the median that holds 99% of the pairs.
Sample (@RG SM) of the accumulation unit. Empty on the ALL_READS row.
Library (@RG LB) of the accumulation unit. Empty on ALL_READS and SAMPLE rows.
Platform unit (@RG PU) of the read group. Empty except on READ_GROUP rows.
Which reads the row counts: UNPAIRED, FIRST_OF_PAIR, SECOND_OF_PAIR, or PAIR for both mates together.
Primary reads in the category, passing filter or not. Secondary and supplementary alignments are not counted. A PAIR row counts both mates.
Reads without the QC-fail flag (0x200).
PF_READS / TOTAL_READS.
PF reads that carry the tag XN=1, the Illumina noise-read mark. The bases are not inspected.
PF reads with a mapped primary alignment, at any mapping quality.
PF_READS_ALIGNED / PF_READS.
Bases of PF aligned reads inside alignment blocks (M, = and X CIGAR operations).
PF aligned reads with mapping quality 20 or more.
Aligned bases of the PF_HQ_ALIGNED_READS.
PF_HQ_ALIGNED_BASES whose base quality is 20 or more.

Median over all PF aligned reads of the mismatches counted in mapping quality 20 or more alignments. A read below mapping quality 20 enters as 0, so many low-quality reads pull the median toward 0. Needs REFERENCE_SEQUENCE, else 0.
Mismatching bases / PF_ALIGNED_BASES, over all PF aligned reads.
Mismatching bases / PF_HQ_ALIGNED_BASES, over the mapping quality 20 or more reads.
Insertion and deletion events (CIGAR I and D operations, not bases) per aligned base: (insertions + deletions) / PF_ALIGNED_BASES. A fraction, not multiplied by 100.
Mean length of the stored sequence of all PF reads, mapped or not. Soft-clipped bases count; hard-clipped bases do not, because they are absent from the record.
Standard deviation of the stored sequence lengths of all PF reads. Soft-clipped bases count; hard-clipped bases do not.
Median stored sequence length of all PF reads. Soft-clipped bases count; hard-clipped bases do not.
Median absolute deviation of the stored sequence lengths of all PF reads (soft clips included, hard clips not).
Shortest stored sequence among PF reads. Soft-clipped bases count; hard-clipped bases do not.
Longest stored sequence among PF reads. Soft-clipped bases count; hard-clipped bases do not.

Mean, over all PF reads, of the bases in M, I, = and X operations; clipped bases are left out. Unmapped PF reads enter as 0 and insertions count, so the value is lower than the mean aligned-block length.
PF aligned reads whose mate is mapped too.
READS_ALIGNED_IN_PAIRS / PF_READS_ALIGNED.
PF aligned primary reads that are paired (flag 0x1) but lack the proper-pair flag (0x2). Unpaired reads never count.
PF_READS_IMPROPER_PAIRS / PF_READS_ALIGNED.

Machine cycles where no-calls reach 80% of the category's TOTAL_READS, QC-failed reads included in the denominator. On PF aligned reads a mismatch to the reference also counts as a bad call. The PAIR row is the sum of FIRST_OF_PAIR and SECOND_OF_PAIR.
PF reads aligned to the forward strand / PF_READS_ALIGNED.

Share of PF aligned primary reads that look chimeric, among those that qualify. A read with a mapped mate qualifies when both ends have mapping quality 20 or more, or its MQ tag is missing; any other read qualifies at mapping quality 20 or more. It is chimeric when |TLEN| exceeds MAX_INSERT_SIZE (default 100000), the mate is on another contig, the orientation is outside EXPECTED_PAIR_ORIENTATIONS (default FR), or the read itself has an SA tag.
Share of PF reads that are unmapped or mapping quality 0 and begin with a known adapter sequence.
Soft-clipped bases of PF mapped primary reads / total bases of all PF reads (stored sequence length, unmapped reads included). The denominator is not PF_ALIGNED_BASES.
Hard-clipped bases (CIGAR H) of PF primary reads / total bases of all PF reads (stored sequence length). The hard-clipped bases are not in the denominator, and PF_ALIGNED_BASES is not used.

Each target goes into one whole-percent GC bin by its own GC. Over bins 0 to 50, sum (share of target bases in the bin - share of high-quality on-target bases in the bin) where positive, times 100. Value is a percentage (0 to 100), not a fraction. 0 when no reference is given.
The AT_DROPOUT sum over bins 50 to 100. Bin 50 is in both sums. A percentage (0 to 100), measured in high-quality on-target bases, not reads. 0 when no reference is given.

Modelled probability of calling a heterozygous SNP at a log-odds threshold of 3, from the depth distribution of target bases (depth capped at COVERAGE_CAP) and the quality distribution of on-target bases. GC content of the window, in percent from 0 to 100; one row per value.
Reference windows of SCAN_WINDOW_SIZE (100) bases with this GC content. Windows with five or more N, and the first and last window of each contig, are not counted.

Mapped reads assigned to a window with this GC content: the window at the alignment start, or for a reverse-strand read the window that ends at the alignment end. Reads whose window starts before base 1 or has five or more N are not counted.

Phred-scaled rate of mismatches plus inserted and deleted bases against the reference, over the bases of the reads assigned to these windows. It does not use the base qualities in the file, and it is 0 when the bin has no error.
Read starts per window in this bin divided by read starts per window over the whole reference. 1 is average.
Half-width of the error bar of NORMALIZED_COVERAGE from the read start count: NORMALIZED_COVERAGE / sqrt(READ_STARTS).

Library (@RG LB) the row describes. Reads without a library are listed as "Unknown Library" by CollectDuplicateMetrics and as "Unknown" by EstimateLibraryComplexity, which also files any pair whose read name has no tile, x and y there.
Mapped primary reads that are unpaired (no pair flag) or whose mate is unmapped. Always 0 from EstimateLibraryComplexity.

CollectDuplicateMetrics and MarkDuplicates: pairs with both mates mapped, primary records only, counted per record and halved. EstimateLibraryComplexity: pairs that passed its quality check, mapped or not, in set sizes seen at least MIN_GROUP_COUNT times.
Mapped secondary or supplementary records, left out of the other counts. An unmapped record counts only in UNMAPPED_READS. Always 0 from EstimateLibraryComplexity.
Records with the unmapped flag, whatever their secondary or supplementary flags. Always 0 from EstimateLibraryComplexity.

CollectDuplicateMetrics: examined pairs whose records carry the duplicate flag. MarkDuplicates: examined pairs it flagged, optical ones included, counted per record and halved. EstimateLibraryComplexity: in each set of identical pairs, every pair after the first.

Duplicate pairs within OPTICAL_DUPLICATE_PIXEL_DISTANCE of another pair on the same tile. Found among the pairs of each duplicate set against the pair kept. 0 from CollectDuplicateMetrics, which has no read positions.

Fraction of examined reads that are duplicates, from 0 to 1 (0.25 is 25%): (UNPAIRED_READ_DUPLICATES + 2 x READ_PAIR_DUPLICATES) / (UNPAIRED_READS_EXAMINED + 2 x READ_PAIRS_EXAMINED). 0 when nothing was examined.

Distinct molecules in the library, from the Lander-Waterman equation over the non-optical pairs and the unique pairs (pairs minus duplicates), truncated to a whole number. Empty when there are no pairs or no duplicate pair beyond the optical ones.
1 for unpaired and first-of-pair records, 2 for second-of-pair records. Secondary and supplementary records are not counted, and PF_READS_ONLY and ALIGNED_READS_ONLY narrow the rest.

Sequencing cycle, 1-based, with reverse-strand records flipped. READ_END 2 cycles are numbered after the last READ_END 1 cycle, so the first base of the second read prints as the first read's length plus 1.

PRO_ALT_BASES + CON_ALT_BASES summed over the same rows.
ALT_COUNT / (REF_COUNT + ALT_COUNT); 0 when both are 0.
Histogram key: insert size in bases.

Pairs with this insert size and FR orientation in the unit named before the dot (All_Reads, or the sample, library or read group PU). Sizes above the trim width (median + DEVIATIONS x MAD, or HISTOGRAM_WIDTH) are not listed, so the column can sum to less than READ_PAIRS.
As for fr_count, with RF: sizes above the trim width are not listed, so the column can sum to less than READ_PAIRS.
As for fr_count, with TANDEM: sizes above the trim width are not listed, so the column can sum to less than READ_PAIRS.
Histogram key: a length in bases. For the *_TOTAL_LENGTH_COUNT columns it is the read length; for the *_ALIGNED_LENGTH_COUNT columns it is the aligned length (M, I, = and X bases).
Primary PF paired reads (both mates) with this stored sequence length. Soft-clipped bases count; hard-clipped bases do not.
PF paired reads (both mates) with this many bases in M, I, = and X operations. Soft and hard clips are left out, insertions count, and unmapped reads fall in the key 0 bin.
Primary PF unpaired reads with this stored sequence length. Soft-clipped bases count; hard-clipped bases do not.
PF unpaired reads with this many bases in M, I, = and X operations. Soft and hard clips are left out, insertions count, and unmapped reads fall in the key 0 bin.
Histogram key: a depth for high_quality_coverage_count, a base quality for unfiltered_baseq_count.
Target bases whose high-quality depth equals the key.

On-target bases with this base quality, from reads that pass the duplicate, adapter and MAPQ filters, after mate-overlap clipping but before the MINIMUM_BASE_QUALITY filter. Bases at quality 2 or below and inserted bases are left out. No coverage cap is applied.
Histogram key: a sequencing multiple from 1 to 100.
Expected multiple of today's unique pairs seen after sequencing BIN times as many pairs, from ESTIMATED_LIBRARY_SIZE. Written only when the file has one library and that library has a size estimate.
Histogram key: a sequencing multiple from 1 to 100 when the file has one library with a size estimate; the set_size columns share it.
Histogram key: the number of pairs in a duplicate set, when the file has no CoverageMult column.
Expected multiple of today's unique pairs seen after sequencing BIN times as many pairs, from ESTIMATED_LIBRARY_SIZE. Written only when the file has one library and that library has a size estimate.
Duplicate sets of pairs with this many pairs, over every library. A pair with no duplicate is a set of 1. Only sets of 1 count when READ_NAME_REGEX is null.
Duplicate sets of pairs with this many optical duplicates plus one.
Duplicate sets of pairs by set size less their optical duplicates.
Histogram key: the number of pairs in a duplicate set.

Per library (the label is the library name): number of groups of identical pairs of this size. Size 1 counts pairs with no duplicate, and every size is listed, including those under MIN_GROUP_COUNT that the metrics row leaves out.
Histogram key: a Phred base quality.
Bases with this QUAL value, in primary records only. N bases are left out unless INCLUDE_NO_CALLS is true; PF_READS_ONLY and ALIGNED_READS_ONLY narrow the reads.
Bases with this OQ value, counted on the same bases as COUNT_OF_Q (primary records, no N unless INCLUDE_NO_CALLS). Present only when a counted base had an OQ.
Histogram key: sequencing cycle, 1-based; second-of-pair cycles follow the first-of-pair ones.
Mean QUAL of the bases at this cycle, over primary records only; PF_READS_ONLY and ALIGNED_READS_ONLY narrow the reads. N bases are included.
Mean OQ of the bases at this cycle, over the same primary records as MEAN_QUALITY and only those that carry OQ. Present only when a counted record had an OQ; 0 at a cycle without one.
Histogram key: a high-quality depth, or a base quality for unfiltered_baseq_count.
Loci whose high-quality depth equals the key. Keys run from 0 to COVERAGE_CAP, empty bins included, and the last key also holds every deeper locus.
Bases with this quality among those feeding the unfiltered depth, before the base quality and overlap filters; quality 2 or less is left out. Written with INCLUDE_BQ_HISTOGRAM=true.
Histogram key: a high-quality depth, or a base quality for unfiltered_baseq_count.
Loci whose high-quality depth equals the key. Keys run from 0 to COVERAGE_CAP, empty bins included, and the last key also holds every deeper locus.
Bases with this quality among those feeding the unfiltered depth, before the base quality and overlap filters; quality 2 or less is left out. Written with INCLUDE_BQ_HISTOGRAM=true.
Histogram key: a high-quality depth, or a base quality for unfiltered_baseq_count.
Loci whose high-quality depth equals the key, every counted locus included. Keys start at 0 and list empty bins, and the last key (COVERAGE_CAP) also holds every deeper locus.
Loci whose high-quality depth equals the key, from depth 1 up. The last key (COVERAGE_CAP) also holds every deeper locus.
Bases with this quality among those feeding the unfiltered depth, before the base quality and overlap filters; quality 2 or less is left out. Written with INCLUDE_BQ_HISTOGRAM=true.
Histogram key: a depth for high_quality_coverage_count, a base quality for unfiltered_baseq_count.
Target bases whose high-quality depth equals the key. The columns repeat once per accumulation unit.

On-target bases with this base quality, from reads that pass the duplicate, adapter and MAPQ filters, after mate-overlap clipping but before the MINIMUM_BASE_QUALITY filter. Bases at quality 2 or below and inserted bases are left out. No coverage cap is applied.
Histogram key: position along the transcript in percent of its length, 0 at the 5' end to 100 at the 3' end.

Coverage within 0.5% of the transcript length around this position, divided by the transcript's mean coverage, averaged over the picked transcripts of the unit named before the dot (All_Reads, or the read group, library or sample). 1 is flat; the last base of each alignment block is not counted.
Every @RG sample of the input joined with commas, in Java HashSet order; UnknownSample stands for a read group without SM. The same text on every row.
The library this row counts: an @RG LB value, or UnknownLibrary for a read group without LB.
The reference context: CONTEXT_SIZE bases (default 1) on each side of a central C, upper case. A G site is read on the other strand, so its context is reverse-complemented.
Reference C and G sites in this context where at least one base of this library passed the read filters and MINIMUM_QUALITY_SCORE and was a reference or alternate base.
Reference and alternate bases counted at those sites: REF_TOTAL_BASES + ALT_NONOXO_BASES + ALT_OXO_BASES. Any other base is not counted.
Reference bases sequenced as C in read 1 or as G in read 2 (the base as the sequencer read it, complemented back on the reverse strand): the orientation oxidation of G cannot produce.
Reference bases sequenced as G in read 1 or as C in read 2: the orientation in which 8-oxoguanine damage would show.
REF_NONOXO_BASES + REF_OXO_BASES.
Alternate bases (A at a C site, T at a G site) sequenced as A in read 1 or as T in read 2: substitutions in the orientation oxidation does not produce, taken as the background error.
Alternate bases sequenced as T in read 1 or as A in read 2: G to T substitutions in the orientation 8-oxoguanine damage produces.
max(ALT_OXO_BASES - ALT_NONOXO_BASES, 1) / TOTAL_BASES: the excess of oxo-oriented substitutions over the background. ? when TOTAL_BASES is 0.
-10 * log10(OXIDATION_ERROR_RATE), a Phred score: lower means more oxidative damage. -? when TOTAL_BASES is 0.
Reference bases counted at sites whose reference base is C.
Reference bases counted at sites whose reference base is G.
Alternate bases (A) counted at sites whose reference base is C.
Alternate bases (T) counted at sites whose reference base is G.
The alternate fraction at C sites minus the alternate fraction at G sites, raised to 1e-10 (printed 0): substitutions biased to C reference sites. ? when either side has no counted base.
-10 * log10(C_REF_OXO_ERROR_RATE); 100 at the 1e-10 floor.
The alternate fraction at G sites minus the alternate fraction at C sites, raised to 1e-10 (printed 0): substitutions biased to G reference sites. ? when either side has no counted base.
-10 * log10(G_REF_OXO_ERROR_RATE); 100 at the 1e-10 floor.
Bases in the merged target intervals (overlapping and abutting targets merged, as CollectHsMetrics merges them).
Number of merged targets; the denominator of PCT_TARGETS_COMPLETE.
The MIN_DEPTH option (default 20): a target base at or above this high-quality depth is reportable.
Target bases whose high-quality depth, as CollectHsMetrics PER_BASE_COVERAGE counts it, is at or above MIN_DEPTH.
BASES_AT_OR_ABOVE_MIN_DEPTH divided by TARGET_TERRITORY. At MIN_DEPTH 20 this equals PCT_TARGET_BASES_20X of CollectHsMetrics on the same input and filters. ? when the territory is 0.
Target bases below MIN_DEPTH: TARGET_TERRITORY minus BASES_AT_OR_ABOVE_MIN_DEPTH.
Number of gap runs: maximal runs of consecutive bases of one merged target below MIN_DEPTH.
Length in bases of the longest gap run; 0 without a gap.
Merged targets that hold at least one gap run.
Merged targets without a gap run, divided by TARGET_COUNT. ? when there is no target.
Histogram key: the length in bases of a gap run.
Number of gap runs of this length.

Primary mapped reads on the autosomes (chr1 to chr22 or 1 to 22, or the AUTOSOMES option) that are not duplicates or QC failures and have MAPQ at or above MINIMUM_MAPPING_QUALITY. With TARGET_INTERVALS, only reads over a target.
Reads counted as for AUTOSOME_READS on the X contig (chrX or X, or X_CONTIG).
Reads counted as for AUTOSOME_READS on the Y contig (chrY or Y, or Y_CONTIG).
Bases of the autosomes: the @SQ lengths summed, or with TARGET_INTERVALS the merged target bases on them.
Bases of the X contig: its @SQ length, or with TARGET_INTERVALS the merged target bases on it.
Bases of the Y contig: its @SQ length, or with TARGET_INTERVALS the merged target bases on it.
X reads per X base divided by autosome reads per autosome base. Near 1 for two X chromosomes, near 0.5 for one. ? when a length or the autosome read count is 0.
Y reads per Y base divided by autosome reads per autosome base. Near 0 without a Y chromosome. ? when a length or the autosome read count is 0.
FEMALE when X_RATIO is at least 0.75 and Y_RATIO under 0.05; MALE when X_RATIO is between 0.3 and 0.75 and Y_RATIO at least 0.1; UNKNOWN otherwise. Starting values (docs/06).
The EXPECTED_SEX option, upper-cased; empty when none was given.
Y when INFERRED_SEX equals DECLARED_SEX, N when the inferred sex is MALE or FEMALE and differs; empty without a declaration or when the inferred sex is UNKNOWN.
Why INFERRED_SEX is UNKNOWN (a contig set with no bases, no autosome reads, or ratios that fit neither pattern), and why SEX_MATCH is empty with a declaration; empty otherwise.

First-of-pair records whose pair is outward facing (RF) on one contig, both mates mapped at or above MINIMUM_MAPPING_QUALITY, with |TLEN| at or below the chimera size. Secondary, supplementary, QC-failed and duplicate records count.
JUMP_PAIRS whose first-of-pair record carries the duplicate flag.
JUMP_DUPLICATE_PAIRS / JUMP_PAIRS, a fraction; 0 without jump pairs.

Lander-Waterman estimate of distinct outward-facing molecules from JUMP_PAIRS and JUMP_PAIRS - JUMP_DUPLICATE_PAIRS (DuplicationMetrics.estimateLibrarySize, truncated); 0 without jump pairs or without jump duplicates.
Mean |TLEN| of the jump pairs over the histogram cut by TAIL_LIMIT: every bin up to the mode, then the consecutive bins holding at least mode count / TAIL_LIMIT pairs. ? without jump pairs.
Sample standard deviation (n - 1) of |TLEN| over the same cut histogram as JUMP_MEAN_INSERT_SIZE. -0 without jump pairs, ? with one.

First-of-pair records whose pair is inward facing (FR) on one contig, both mates mapped at or above MINIMUM_MAPPING_QUALITY, with |TLEN| at or below the chimera size. Secondary, supplementary, QC-failed and duplicate records count.
NONJUMP_PAIRS whose first-of-pair record carries the duplicate flag.
NONJUMP_DUPLICATE_PAIRS / NONJUMP_PAIRS, a fraction; 0 without non-jump pairs.
Lander-Waterman estimate of distinct inward-facing molecules from NONJUMP_PAIRS and NONJUMP_PAIRS - NONJUMP_DUPLICATE_PAIRS; 0 without non-jump pairs or without non-jump duplicates.
Mean |TLEN| of the non-jump pairs over the histogram cut by TAIL_LIMIT as for JUMP_MEAN_INSERT_SIZE. ? without non-jump pairs.
Sample standard deviation (n - 1) of |TLEN| over the same cut histogram as NONJUMP_MEAN_INSERT_SIZE. -0 without non-jump pairs, ? with one.

First-of-pair records, both mates mapped and passing the mapping quality test, with |TLEN| above the greater of CHIMERA_KB_MIN and the mode of the first 50000 outward-facing pairs sampled, or on the same strand as the mate, or on another contig than the mate.
First-of-pair records with exactly one mate mapped: the read unmapped and the mate mapped, or the read mapped and the mate unmapped. Not subject to the mapping quality test.
JUMP_PAIRS / (JUMP_PAIRS + NONJUMP_PAIRS + CHIMERIC_PAIRS), a fraction; 0 without any.
NONJUMP_PAIRS / (JUMP_PAIRS + NONJUMP_PAIRS + CHIMERIC_PAIRS), a fraction; 0 without any.
CHIMERIC_PAIRS / (JUMP_PAIRS + NONJUMP_PAIRS + CHIMERIC_PAIRS), a fraction; 0 without any.
The mitochondrial contig: MT_CONTIG, else the one of chrM, MT, M or chrMT in the header.
Bases of the mitochondrial contig: its @SQ length less the merged EXCLUDE_INTERVALS on it. TARGET_INTERVALS do not change it.

Aligned bases (M, = and X operations; soft clips, insertions and deletions add nothing) at or above MINIMUM_BASE_QUALITY on the mitochondrial contig, outside EXCLUDE_INTERVALS, of primary mapped reads that are not duplicates or QC failures and have MAPQ at or above MINIMUM_MAPPING_QUALITY.
MT_BASES / MT_LENGTH. ? when MT_LENGTH is 0.
Bases of the autosomes (chr1 to chr22 or 1 to 22, or the AUTOSOMES option): the @SQ lengths summed, or with TARGET_INTERVALS the merged target bases on them, less the merged EXCLUDE_INTERVALS.
Bases counted as for MT_BASES inside the AUTOSOMAL_LENGTH territory.
AUTOSOMAL_BASES / AUTOSOMAL_LENGTH. ? when AUTOSOMAL_LENGTH is 0.

2 x MT_MEAN_DEPTH / AUTOSOMAL_MEAN_DEPTH: mitochondrial genomes per diploid nuclear genome. With TARGET_INTERVALS on an exome the mitochondrial reads are off target and the value is a ratio, not a copy number. ? when the autosomal depth is 0.
Reads that added at least one base to MT_BASES or AUTOSOMAL_BASES.
Sample (@RG SM) of the accumulation unit. Empty on the ALL_READS row.
Library (@RG LB) of the accumulation unit. Empty on ALL_READS and SAMPLE rows.
Platform unit (@RG PU) of the read group. Empty except on READ_GROUP rows.
The gene_name of the exon's gene (GFF3: the gene's Name), else its gene_id. BED12 and BED: the line's name.
The gene_id of the exon's gene, as written. BED12 and BED: the line's name.
The transcript_id the exon belongs to, as written. BED12 and BED: the line's name. An exon of two transcripts has a row for each.

The exon_number (GFF3: rank) written in the annotation; without one, the exon's place along the transcript from its 5' end, so the exon with the highest start is 1 on the minus strand. Overlapping exons of one transcript merge and keep the lowest number.
The contig as the BAM header names it; the annotation's name when the header lacks the contig.
First base of the exon, 1-based (a BED start plus 1).
Last base of the exon, 1-based and included.
+, - or . as the annotation writes the strand.
Bases of the exon: END minus START plus 1.

Sum of the high-quality depth of the exon's bases divided by LENGTH. The depth is the one CollectHsMetrics writes to PER_BASE_COVERAGE, so this equals the mean_coverage column of PER_TARGET_COVERAGE for the same interval. Empty when the BAM header lacks the contig.
The middle depth of the exon's bases; the mean of the two middle depths when LENGTH is even.
The lowest depth of a base of the exon; equals the min_coverage column of CollectHsMetrics PER_TARGET_COVERAGE for the same interval.
The highest depth of a base of the exon.
Bases of the exon with a depth of at least N, one column per MIN_DEPTH value (default 10, 20 and 30).
BASES_<N>X divided by LENGTH.
GENE for the union of the selected exons of one gene on one contig, TRANSCRIPT for the exons of one transcript. Each gene row comes first, then the rows of its transcripts.
The gene_name of the gene (GFF3: its Name), else its gene_id.
The gene_id of the gene, as written.
The transcript of a TRANSCRIPT row; empty on a GENE row.
The contig as the BAM header names it; the annotation's name when the header lacks the contig. A gene on two contigs has a row per contig.
The lowest exon start of the row, 1-based.
The highest exon end of the row, 1-based and included.
The strand of the row's first exon in the annotation.
Distinct exon intervals of the row; an exon two transcripts share counts once on the GENE row.
Bases of the union of the row's exons, so a base two transcripts share counts once on the GENE row. Introns are not counted.
Sum of the high-quality depth of the LENGTH bases divided by LENGTH, with the depth of ExonCoverageMetrics. Empty when the BAM header lacks the contig.
The middle depth of the LENGTH bases; the mean of the two middle depths when LENGTH is even.
The lowest depth of a base of the row's exons.
The highest depth of a base of the row's exons.
Bases of the row's exons with a depth of at least N, one column per MIN_DEPTH value (default 10, 20 and 30).
BASES_<N>X divided by LENGTH.
Adapter name: one of FastQC's six (Configuration/adapter_list.txt), or the NAME of an ADAPTER_SEQUENCE value (the sequence itself when no name is given).
The bases searched: the adapter's first ADAPTER_KMER bases (default 12), upper case. A read carries the adapter when they occur in it exactly.
FIRST (flags 0x1 and 0x40 without 0x80), SECOND (0x1 and 0x80 without 0x40) or UNPAIRED (any other record). Only read ends with a counted record get rows.
Primary records of the read end, unmapped included; secondary and supplementary never count, QC-failed records leave with PF_READS_ONLY and duplicates with INCLUDE_DUPLICATES=false.
Reads whose bases in sequencing order (reverse complemented for flag 0x10) hold KMER at any position.
100 x READS_WITH_ADAPTER / READS, a percent from 0 to 100. ? without a read.
Mean 1-based cycle at which KMER first starts, over READS_WITH_ADAPTER. ? when no read has the adapter.

The by-cycle histogram's value at its last cycle: 100 x reads whose KMER starts at or before that cycle / READS, the value FastQC grades (warn above 5, fail above 10). Equals PCT_READS_WITH_ADAPTER unless a read is longer than 1,000 cycles plus the key.

Proper pairs (flags 0x1 and 0x2, both mates mapped, TLEN not 0) of the read end whose abs(TLEN) is below the record's read length, over all such pairs: a fraction from 0 to 1 that needs no sequence search. ? without a proper pair.
Sample (@RG SM) of the accumulation unit. Empty on the ALL_READS rows.
Library (@RG LB) of the accumulation unit. Empty on ALL_READS and SAMPLE rows.
Platform unit (@RG PU) of the read group. Empty except on READ_GROUP rows.
Histogram key: the 1-based cycle in sequencing order, from 1 to the last cycle at which KMER can start in the longest read (read length - ADAPTER_KMER + 1), at most 1,000.

Cumulative percent (0 to 100) of the reads of the unit, read end and adapter named by the label (unit.READ_END.ADAPTER) whose KMER starts at or before this cycle: FastQC's Adapter Content curve. ? for a read end without a read in the unit.
What the row sums: TILE (one flowcell lane and tile), LANE (the tiles of one flowcell lane), UNPARSED (reads whose name gave no tile under READ_NAME_REGEX) or ALL (every counted read).
The third field of a 7-field Illumina name; empty for a 5-field name, with a READ_NAME_REGEX, and on UNPARSED and ALL rows.
The field before the tile in a 5- or 7-field Illumina name, as written; empty with a READ_NAME_REGEX and on UNPARSED and ALL rows.
The tile from the read name as MarkDuplicates reads it (cut to 16 bits); empty except on TILE rows.
Records counted: every unmapped record and every mapped record that is neither secondary nor supplementary. Both mates of a pair count.
Unmapped records, counted before the secondary and supplementary test as CollectDuplicateMetrics counts UNMAPPED_READS.
Mapped primary records that are unpaired or whose mate is unmapped, as UNPAIRED_READS_EXAMINED.
Pairs with both mates mapped, counted once on the first-of-pair primary record, as READ_PAIRS_EXAMINED.
UNPAIRED_READS that carry the duplicate flag, as UNPAIRED_READ_DUPLICATES.
PAIRS whose first-of-pair record carries the duplicate flag, as READ_PAIR_DUPLICATES.
Duplicate reads: UNPAIRED_DUPLICATES + 2 x PAIR_DUPLICATES.

PAIR_DUPLICATES whose first-of-pair record carries DT:Z:SQ (MarkDuplicates TAGGING_POLICY=All or OpticalOnly), as READ_PAIR_OPTICAL_DUPLICATES. Empty when no duplicate carries a DT tag and no MarkDuplicates @PG line sets TAGGING_POLICY to All or OpticalOnly.
DUPLICATES / (UNPAIRED_READS + 2 x PAIRS), a fraction, as PERCENT_DUPLICATION; 0 without an examined read.
OPTICAL_DUPLICATES / PAIRS, a fraction; 0 without a pair, empty when OPTICAL_DUPLICATES is.

The lane's median PCT_DUPLICATION over its tiles that examined a read, plus the larger of OUTLIER_SD x 1.4826 x their median absolute deviation and 0.005; on the lane's TILE and LANE rows. Empty with fewer than 3 such tiles.
Y when the tile's PCT_DUPLICATION is above OUTLIER_LIMIT, N when not; empty on other rows, for a tile that examined no read and without a limit.
Smallest x coordinate in the read names of the row; empty on UNPARSED rows.
Largest x coordinate in the read names of the row; empty on UNPARSED rows.
Smallest y coordinate in the read names of the row; empty on UNPARSED rows.
Largest y coordinate in the read names of the row; empty on UNPARSED rows.
On the ALL row: a file with no duplicate flag and no duplicate marker @PG line, an empty OPTICAL_DUPLICATES and how to fill it, and the count of UNPARSED reads; joined by "; ". Empty elsewhere.

Primary records of the unit that are not QC failures and hold at least one base, unmapped ones included; duplicates only with COUNT_DUPLICATES=true. Secondary and supplementary records are not counted.

Reads of TOTAL_READS holding at least TELOMERE_REPEAT_THRESHOLD (default 7, TelSeq's k) non-overlapping copies of REPEAT (default TTAGGG) or of its reverse complement (CCCTAA), counted on the read as sequenced; the larger of the two counts is the read's repeat count.
TELOMERIC_READS / TOTAL_READS. ? when TOTAL_READS is 0.
Reads of TOTAL_READS whose G plus C count is over 48 and at most 52 percent of the read length, N bases included in the length: TelSeq's GC bins 0.48 to 0.52, the denominator of the length estimate.
The most common read length among TOTAL_READS, the shorter on a tie. The histogram runs from 0 to READ_LENGTH divided by the REPEAT length. Empty when TOTAL_READS is 0.
Fraction of TOTAL_READS whose length differs from READ_LENGTH by more than 10 percent of READ_LENGTH. Over 0.05 empties ESTIMATED_LENGTH_KB. ? when TOTAL_READS is 0.

TelSeq's mean telomere length in kb: TELOMERIC_READS / READS_GC_48_52 x GENOME_LENGTH_AT_GC (default 332720800) / 1000 / TELOMERE_ENDS (default 46). Empty when READS_GC_48_52 is 0 or PCT_OFF_LENGTH is over 0.05. Calibrated for human whole genomes of one read length; on an exome it is a ratio, not a length.
Sample (@RG SM) of the accumulation unit. Empty on the ALL_READS row.
Library (@RG LB) of the accumulation unit. Empty on the ALL_READS and SAMPLE rows.
Platform unit (@RG PU) of the read group. Empty except on READ_GROUP rows.
Histogram key: a read's repeat count, the larger of its non-overlapping REPEAT and reverse complement counts, from 0 to READ_LENGTH divided by the REPEAT length, and higher for longer reads.
Reads with this repeat count in the unit named before the dot (All_Reads, or the sample, library or read group PU): TelSeq's TEL0, TEL1, ... columns.
The reference, in BAM header order; empty on a group row and on the ALL row.

The contig group by name: AUTOSOME (chr1 to chr22, 1 to 22), X, Y, MT (chrM, MT, M, chrMT), ALT (_alt), DECOY (_decoy, hs37d5), HLA (HLA-) or OTHER. A row with an empty CONTIG sums its group; ALL sums every reference.
The reference length from the BAM header, summed over the group on a group row.
Records placed on the reference without the unmapped flag, from the index metadata: duplicates, secondary and supplementary records, QC failures and MAPQ 0 included.
Records placed on the reference with the unmapped flag (usually the mate of a mapped read), from the index metadata.
MAPPED x READ_LENGTH / LENGTH: an estimate with no filter, no clip and no overlap removed. ? when LENGTH is 0 or the read length is unknown; 0 when MAPPED is 0.

MAPPED per base of the row divided by MAPPED per base of the autosomes; the read length cancels. On the X and Y group rows it is the X and Y ratio CollectSexCheckMetrics compares; ? without autosome reads.
The mean read length of the mapped primary records with a sequence among the first READ_LENGTH_SAMPLE records, or READ_LENGTH when given; empty when no record qualified.
On the ALL row: records with no reference, the count after the last reference of the index.
On the ALL row: FEMALE, MALE or UNKNOWN from the X and Y ratios, with the thresholds of CollectSexCheckMetrics.

On the ALL row: 2 x the RATIO_TO_AUTOSOMES of the MT group, the mitochondrial copy number estimate of CollectMtCopyNumberMetrics from unfiltered records; ? without a mitochondrial contig or autosome reads.
On the ALL row: why INFERRED_SEX is UNKNOWN, why MT_COPY_NUMBER or the depths are ?; empty when every value is defined.
Records counted: every record, mapped or not; secondary and supplementary records only when their INCLUDE option is set.
Counted records without the QC-fail flag (0x200).
TOTAL_BASES / TOTAL_READS, integer division; 0 without reads.
Bases in the counted records.
Bases in PF records.
Bases with quality 20 or more: QUAL, or the ALTERNATE_QUALITY_ATTRIBUTE tag decoded as Phred+33.
Q20 bases in PF records.
Bases with quality 30 or more; each is also a Q20 base.
Q30 bases in PF records.
Bases with quality 40 or more; each is also a Q20 and a Q30 base.
Q40 bases in PF records.
Q20_BASES / TOTAL_BASES; 0 without bases.
Q30_BASES / TOTAL_BASES; 0 without bases.
Q40_BASES / TOTAL_BASES; 0 without bases.
PF_Q20_BASES / PF_BASES; 0 without PF bases.
PF_Q30_BASES / PF_BASES; 0 without PF bases.
PF_Q40_BASES / PF_BASES; 0 without PF bases.
SNV quality observations: at each base, one from each of the qa, qc, qg and qt tags whose base (A, C, G, T) it is not. An A, C, G or T base gives 3, an N or other code 4.
SNV quality observations in PF records.
SNV quality observations of 20 or more (the tag character minus 33).
Q20 SNV quality observations in PF records.
SNV quality observations of 30 or more; each is also a Q20 one.
Q30 SNV quality observations in PF records.
SNV quality observations of 40 or more; each is also a Q20 and a Q30 one.
Q40 SNV quality observations in PF records.
Q20_SNVQ / TOTAL_SNVQ; 0 without observations.
Q30_SNVQ / TOTAL_SNVQ; 0 without observations.
Q40_SNVQ / TOTAL_SNVQ; 0 without observations.
PF_Q20_SNVQ / PF_SNVQ; 0 without PF observations.
PF_Q30_SNVQ / PF_SNVQ; 0 without PF observations.
PF_Q40_SNVQ / PF_SNVQ; 0 without PF observations.
Histogram key (INCLUDE_BQ_HISTOGRAM): a quality for BQ_COUNT and SNVQ_COUNT, a 0-based read index for the two means; one column of keys holds both.
Counted bases with this base quality.
SNV quality observations with this value.
Mean base quality at this read index, in stored order (a reverse-strand read is not reversed), over every counted record long enough.
